Bid rules will be modified to allow units to indicate an upper MW limit, separate from the Upper Operating Limit (UOL), that will be honored in the scheduling horizon by SCUC, BME and SCD under certain environmental and operating situations. Multiple response rates will be allowed. This modification is intended to encourage units to be on dispatch by allowing units to move in response to price signals. MIS will be modified to allow up to three response rate ranges to be entered as static data inputs. Payment rules for start-up will be modified. Payment rules for unforced energy replacement will be modified. Changes to SCUC will be deployed to optimize Phase Angle Regulators (PARs) for evaluation of the Day Ahead Market (DAM).

German bank associations plan to help by pooling credit data for their members. But Mr Schr?der's advice to banks last week was that they should not be overhasty in applying the new Basel principles ahead of time. Already the committee is working on a fix. On November 5th it posted a clutch of new suggestions on its website that included new risk weightings for smaller companies, and proposals that physical collateral, receivables and even leased assets be used to lessen a particular company's credit charge. These were interim ideas, it said, which needed to be tested and even revised. All well and good. But the Basel committee is getting into knots trying to address every objection as it arises.
